delivery_acceptance.scope: This bounded source-admission task only; paper and future baseline remain unfinished.

accepted_decision: Admit C117R3 for one conditional finite ordinary baseline only. No G0/G1, native common-IOMMU, mechanism novelty or performance claim is accepted.
scope: Targeted direct reading of decisive primary source and current hardware interface; no experiment reruns.

findings.fact: The source has useful software VM-to-VM forwarding into another vhost device RX queue. It is distinct from the closed physical-NIC dmafwd staging-copy task.
findings.decision: Accept task provenance; source selection is bounded to this workflow.

findings.fact: Guest refill binds its cookie to the published writable descriptor address; RX completion resolves used ID back to that same cookie.
findings.decision: A pointer swap in the host backend alone does not deliver bytes into the prepublished guest buffer. This establishes movement under the frozen buffer contract, not a universal proof against page remapping or cooperative sharing.

findings.fact: Async enqueue computes source/destination IOV segments from packet data and guest buffer addresses and issues byte-counted DMA copies.
findings.decision: Source-supported payload/copy semantics; DMA is optional because CPU copy remains a valid baseline.

findings.fact: The backend checks DMA packet completion before used-ring release publication/notification; accepted source mbufs remain owned until completion polling permits freeing.
findings.decision: The projected adapter must preserve hold-through-copy, publish-after-completion and consume-before-destination-reuse; DONE alone is not application success.

findings.fact: The official example permits multiple vhost devices and DMA channels, and discusses VFIO/IOVA modes. It does not establish a measured native common physical IOMMU or concurrent traffic trace.
findings.decision: Accept natural actors and source-supported channel configuration; native common-IOMMU state and timing remain unknown. FPGA claims use separately accepted existing shared path only.

findings.fact: The 4096-byte restriction applies to the batch configuration. The ordinary non-batch request carries programmed length/source/destination, accepts nonzero length, and DEFAULT retires after one transfer.
findings.decision: Do not infer hardware inexpressibility from a narrower current driver interface. A bounded finite software adapter is admissible for future implementation, with exact-byte/payload checks still required.

acceptance_conditions: Direct A-to-B CPU and single-DMA copy eliminate the intermediate host staging buffer as the strongest ordinary baselines; this is an allowed adaptation, not asserted to be implemented by current upstream source.
Allow lawful page remapping/shared buffers/cooperative output when address granularity, adjacent data, guest contract and lifetimes actually permit; do not exclude them solely by owner labels.
DMA global-quiet/cache handoff is costed only where required. CPU must not be charged DMA-only barriers for superficial symmetry.
Finite FPGA projection preserves the independent prepublished destination and source lifetime; it drops native VM/network deployment and has no measured traffic-arrival or performance claim.
Source admission authorizes only an inactive bounded ordinary-baseline successor, not G0/G1 or mechanism novelty.
